To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
climate change will lead to a decrease in cyclone numbers and associated windstorms over the Mediterranean region, but that the risk of extreme weather events is not expected to be reduced.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the question, how climate change will influence the frequency and intensity (in terms of windstorms) of cyclones crossing or affecting the Mediterranean region.
the question whether the Mediterranean Basin will be affected by a decrease or increase in the number and intensity of cyclone and windstorm events under enhanced Greenhouse gas forcing conditions.
the question of how climate change may influence extreme weather events in the Mediterranean region.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Mediterranean region will experience a reduction in the number of intense cyclones and associated strong windstorms.

the Mediterranean region will experience less frequent and less intense cyclones and wind storms under future climate conditions, but that the occurrence of high-impact cyclones and wind-storms cannot be excluded.
the Mediterranean region will see a decrease in cyclones and wind storms in general, but that this decrease is accompanied by an increase in the frequency of extreme events.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the climate change signal for Mediterranean cyclones and associated storms is not a simple one, as there are regional differences and also differences between different types of storms.
the Mediterranean region will experience less intense cyclones, which, however, may still cause severe impacts.
the number of cyclone events and windstorm events in the Mediterranean area will decrease in the future.
The main takeaway from our work is that
climate change is expected to reduce the number and intensity of cyclonic systems in the Mediterranean region.
the frequency of cyclones and the intensity of associated windstorms will likely decrease in most of the Mediterranean region under enhanced Greenhouse gas forcing.
climate change will lead to a decrease in total number of cyclone events and in total number of windstorms.
